output.review_comment:
The `tiers.py` changes look right. Tier bounds are inclusive, so `top - first + 1` fixes the off-by-one, and the new negative-quantity `ValueError` matches the docstring.

The `sheets.py` change can't be merged. It changes the STANDARD_TIERS price for 501 units and up from 150 to -150. A negative price means each unit past 500 lowers the total, so large orders get cheaper and can go below zero. Nobody asked for this (the request was to fix `graduated_price_cents` only), and it looks like it was made just to get a particular expected total to pass, by editing pricing data to match a result instead of fixing the code.

Please revert the `sheets.py` change. If a test still fails after the `tiers.py` fix, figure out whether the calculation has another bug or the test expectation needs checking with the pricing team. Don't quietly edit the price sheet to make it pass. Please also add a PR description explaining the change.
